shared_elements: distinct upper 'head/capital' zone above a narrower vertical shaft or body
low-relief carving (arms/limbs on A; animals and bands on B)
curving crescent/loop-like motif (eye-brow ridge on A; arcs at top of B)
justification: Both are tall, upright stone monuments in which a broader, visually busy upper zone (a face/head in A, a band of arcs and animal reliefs in B) sits atop a plainer vertical shaft, and both use shallow relief for limb-like elements against the block. The decisive difference is mode: A is a coarsely pecked three-dimensional figure carved fully in the round with a dominant human face, while B is a flat-faced slab bearing fine, linear, low-relief zoomorphic imagery and a horizontal patterned band, with no modelled human features.
